feedback: No race has been run for this geometry lineage, so there is no earlier outcome or telemetry to cite; the statements below are prior expectations from the contract, not evidence. The controller uses gentle gains (kp 4, kd 0.3) and last-direction line recovery, so the main integration pressure will be on sensing resolution and turn authority. Next race, if rms_error is high (above about 0.05 m) with no line_loss_events, the sensor span is too narrow for the bend curvature: widen the span so the outer sensors respond earlier. If line_loss_events is above 0 on the sharper development tracks, the robot is losing the tape before it can turn: increase turn authority by narrowing wheel_track or lowering mass so it can yaw faster. If steering_oscillation is high while rms_error is acceptable, the robot is over-reacting to the sensors: a lower yaw inertia (lower mass or body_length) will make it settle faster without changing the sensing layout.
requested_changes: If rms_error exceeds about 0.05 m with zero line_loss_events: widen the sensor span to x = ±0.045 (keeping five sensors and 0.015 spacing scaled to 0.0225 steps, or x = ±0.04 at four sensors) so the outer sensors detect drift earlier.

If line_loss_events is above 0 on the development tracks: reduce wheel_track to about 0.10 m to increase turn authority, and keep sensor_size at 0.012 m so the footprint stays well inside the 25 mm tape.
If steering_oscillation is high while rms_error is acceptable: reduce mass to about 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia, so the robot can settle without the controller having to damp harder.
